items.title: Mike Vax interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2022
items.q: Gerry Mulligan only wrote six charts for the Kenton band and Stan didn’t really like that many of them.

ctx.x: I think he did both. I think there were certain writers like Ken Hanna — when I was on the band, Ken Hanna, Willie Maiden, Hank Levy, where Stan just let them pretty much have their own — because they knew what Stan wanted. I mean even you go back to the early writers, Pete Rugulo and Bill Russo and Johnny Richards, they all knew what Stan wanted. And yeah, a lot of times like with “Cuban Fire” which if I had to say even over the albums I’m on, probably my favorite Kenton album, Stan said to Johnny Richards, you…

doing. With Hank Levy’s time charts, you know Stan — Hank Levy had played on Stan’s band in the late 40s I think, played baritone sax and done a little bit of writing. But then of course later on got into a thing with Don Ellis with all the time charts and Stan decided, you know obviously before we did all those in the 70s when Stan recorded “Adventures in Jazz” with Johnny Richards, I mean amazing time charts. But we really got into it with public performance of time charts with Hank. And Stan pretty much gave…
And this ain’t the “Woodchopper’s Ball” here.
